History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
34-year-old man with 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, and a blanching, red, itchy generalized rash after recent travel to Thailand; advised to seek urgent in-person assessment to rule out serious infection (e.g., dengue, meningitis).

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe, persistent headache for 4 days.  
• Timeline:  
  – Day 0: Headache onset.  
  – Day 1–2: Developed subjective fever (“feels hot,” no measured temperature).  
  – Current: Generalized muscle aches, diffuse red itchy rash, feeling cold without frank rigors.  
• Characteristics/Associated symptoms:  
  – No photophobia.  
  – No neck stiffness or pain with neck movement.  
  – No nausea or vomiting.  
  – No cough, coryza, ear pain.  
  – No focal neurological deficits, pins-and-needles, or limb weakness.  
• Exposures/Risk factors: Returned from Thailand ~1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; friend who traveled with him is also unwell.  
• Medications tried for symptom relief: Paracetamol and Ibuprofen with minimal benefit.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No bleeding, no localized rash areas, no non-blanching rash, no photophobia, no motor weakness, no cough/cold symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No past surgeries reported.  
• No regular medications.

Social History:
• Recent travel: Thailand (returned ~1 week ago).  
• Mosquito exposure: Yes.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed/not documented.

Family History:
• Not discussed/not documented.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during virtual visit (patient advised to attend clinic for examination).

Investigations:
• None performed yet; clinician suggests blood tests may be required after in-person evaluation.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Headache with fever, myalgia, blanching rash post-travel  
  – Assessment: Suspected viral illness; differential includes mosquito-borne infection (e.g., dengue) and early meningitis (less likely given blanching rash and absence of photophobia/neck stiffness).  
  – Plan:  
    • Urgent same-day face-to-face assessment at clinic hub.  
    • Possible referral to hospital for further work-up depending on findings.  
    • Likely investigations after examination: full blood count, inflammatory markers, dengue serology/malarial screen, other relevant labs.  
    • Continue symptomatic treatment with Paracetamol and Ibuprofen as needed.  

Issue 2: Diffuse red, itchy, blanching rash  
  – Assessment: Viral exanthem vs. other travel-related rash.  
  – Plan: Evaluate rash during in-person visit; consider dermatologic and infectious etiologies.

General plan items:  
• Red-flag advice: If unable to secure clinic appointment within a few hours, patient to self-present to urgent care or emergency department.  
• Safety-netting: Seek immediate care for worsening headache, development of non-blanching rash, photophobia, neck stiffness, confusion, vomiting, or bleeding manifestations.  
• Follow-up: As per findings after in-person assessment.

Quality checks:
• Expected but missing elements: Objective vitals; physical examination findings; complete social history (occupation, smoking, alcohol); detailed medication reconciliation.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient identified as “John Doe” at start; clinician addresses patient as “Ben” later – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational overlaps; no significant inaudible sections.
